subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Election Interference Online
description: A quick win: understand Election Interference Online.

hook.text: Russia's Internet Research Agency created fake American accounts and ran ads targeting US voters in 2016.

buildup.text: Foreign operatives used Facebook and Instagram to amplify political divisions with fake grassroots content.

discovery.text: The ads reached an estimated 126 million Americans. Most had no idea the content was foreign-created.

twist.text: Platforms profit from political ads regardless of origin. Verifying who buys them wasn't a priority.

climax.text: Social media gave foreign powers a direct channel to manipulate democratic elections — cheaply and at scale.

punchline.text: Foreign ads. American voters. No one checked.

quiz.question: How did Russia's Internet Research Agency interfere with the 2016 US election?
options: By creating fake accounts and running targeted political ads on social media
